cohort: The study included 327 teenage mothers (mean age 18.4 years) delivering at Mbarara Regional Referral Hospital in Uganda.
finding: More than half (59.9%) of teenage mothers experienced adverse maternal obstetrical outcomes, with a prior history of miscarriage being significantly associated with these adverse events.
mod_finding: Having a cesarean delivery was found to significantly reduce the occurrence of adverse maternal obstetric events by 97% among the participants.
cross-section timing: Data was collected post-delivery in the post-delivery ward.
